title: AIFS-DOP: End-to-End Medium-Range Weather Prediction from Observations Alone with Machine Learning
relevance_note: AIFS-DOP: trained on gridded OBSERVATIONS alone, no reanalysis — directly relevant to your finding that ERA5 assimilates your stations.

title: AIFS-SUBS: Extending Data-Driven Forecasting to Sub-Seasonal Timescales
relevance_note: AIFS-SUBS: sub-seasonal AIFS, weeks 2-6, ~200x less inference energy than IFS. Shows the AIFS family is expanding into your lead-time range.

title: AIFS-COMPO: A Global Data-Driven Atmospheric Composition Forecasting System
relevance_note: AIFS-COMPO atmospheric composition — evidence of the modular Anemoi/AIFS ecosystem you could build on.

title: Representing the Surface Ocean in ECMWF's data-driven forecasting system AIFS
relevance_note: AIFS ocean/wave/sea-ice coupling — matters for the Baltic/Barents/White Sea part of your box.

title: AIFS-CRPS: ensemble forecasting using a model trained with a loss function based on the continuous ranked probability score
relevance_note: AIFS-CRPS journal version: 'almost fair CRPS' loss gives a directly-generative ensemble that beats IFS ENS on most variables/lead times. This is the AIFS ENS you would downscale.

title: Huge ensembles – Part 1: Design of ensemble weather forecasts using spherical Fourier neural operators
relevance_note: Huge Ensembles (SFNO, 1.1B params): shows ML ensemble MEMBERS keep constant spectra with lead time while the ensemble MEAN degrades — the correct diagnostic framing for blurring.

title: FourCastNet 3: A geometric approach to probabilistic machine-learning weather forecasting at scale
relevance_note: FourCastNet 3: probabilistic, well-calibrated, RETAINS REALISTIC SPECTRA to 60 days; 60-day 0.25deg forecast in <4 min on one GPU. The counter-example to 'AI models must blur'.

title: An update to ECMWF's machine-learned weather forecast model AIFS
relevance_note: AIFS Single update: physical-consistency bounding layers, expanded variables; states AIFS fully operational at ECMWF since 25 Feb 2025. Essential for knowing which AIFS version you are downloading.

title: FuXi-ENS: A machine learning model for efficient and accurate ensemble weather prediction
relevance_note: FuXi-ENS: CRPS-trained ensemble, an independent line to AIFS-CRPS.

title: Neural general circulation models for weather and climate
relevance_note: NeuralGCM primary (Nature). Hybrid differentiable dynamical core + learned physics; stable multi-decade climate runs at 140 km.

title: Probabilistic weather forecasting with machine learning
relevance_note: GenCast primary (Nature). Diffusion ensemble, 0.25deg/12h, 15 days in 8 min; better than ENS on 97.2% of 1320 targets. The generative-ensemble reference point.

title: AIFS -- ECMWF's data-driven forecasting system
relevance_note: PRIMARY AIFS paper. GNN encoder/decoder + sliding-window transformer, trained on ERA5 + operational analyses; run 4x daily, open data policy. Start here.

title: AIFS-CRPS: Ensemble forecasting using a model trained with a loss function based on the Continuous Ranked Probability Score
relevance_note: arXiv preprint of AIFS-CRPS; fuller methods detail than the journal version in places.

title: WeatherBench 2: A Benchmark for the Next Generation of Data‐Driven Global Weather Models
venue: Journal of Advances in Modeling Earth Systems
relevance_note: WeatherBench 2: the standard evaluation framework and baseline data. Read for metric definitions before you verify anything.

title: GenCast: Diffusion-based ensemble forecasting for medium-range weather
relevance_note: GenCast preprint.

title: Accurate medium-range global weather forecasting with 3D neural networks
relevance_note: Pangu-Weather primary (Nature). 3D Earth-Specific Transformer, 0.25deg, ~256M params, 43 yr ERA5; hierarchical temporal aggregation to limit error accumulation.

title: Learning skillful medium-range global weather forecasting
relevance_note: GraphCast primary (Science). 0.25deg, 10-day, sub-minute inference; beats operational deterministic on 90% of 1380 targets. The GNN template AIFS descends from.

title: FourCastNet: A Global Data-driven High-resolution Weather Model using Adaptive Fourier Neural Operators
relevance_note: FourCastNet primary preprint: adaptive Fourier neural operator, 0.25deg, week-long forecast in <2 s — the cheap-large-ensemble argument.

title: Pangu-Weather: A 3D High-Resolution Model for Fast and Accurate Global Weather Forecast
relevance_note: Pangu preprint; more architecture detail on 3DEST and the greedy multi-timestep scheme.

title: GraphCast: Learning skillful medium-range global weather forecasting
relevance_note: GraphCast preprint version.

title: Extreme Weather Bench: A framework and benchmark for evaluation of high-impact weather
relevance_note: Extreme Weather Bench: community benchmark for high-impact weather; the verification framework to adopt rather than invent.

title: A spectral test of the butterfly effect and physical consistency in the diffusion-based GenCast’s ensembles
relevance_note: Kim et al., spectral test of the butterfly effect and physical consistency in GenCast ensembles — how to test whether a generative ensemble perturbs realistically.

title: Forecasting the Future With Yesterday's Climate: Temperature Bias in AI Weather and Climate Models
relevance_note: Landsberg et al.: AI models are COLD-BIASED, resembling climates 15-20 yr earlier than the predicted period; cold bias strongest at hottest temperatures. A trained-on-history artefact your bias correction would inherit.

title: Verification of AI–based environmental forecasting systems: What can we do, what do we need to do, and what are the challenges?
venue: Journal of the European Meteorological Society.
relevance_note: Broecker et al., what verification of AI-based forecasting systems needs — methodological guardrails for your own evaluation.

title: Do AI weather models miss extremes?
relevance_note: Gabler et al., station-based (not reanalysis-based) extremes verification of 11 systems over Europe, 10 months. AIFS loses 4.9+/-2.0% in the heat tail; ALL models incl. NWP show a shared conditional bias toward the distribution centre. The single most relevant error-mode paper for station-based work.

title: GraphCast Skill and Systematic Biases in Indian Summer Monsoon Forecasts: Evaluation Against ERA5 and IMERG
relevance_note: GraphCast Indian monsoon evaluation: regional power-spectrum variance ratio 0.14 vs IMERG, compressed rainfall intensity distribution — a clean quantification of deterministic smoothing.

title: Physics-based models outperform AI weather forecasts of record-breaking extremes
relevance_note: Zhang et al., Sci Adv 2026: for RECORD-BREAKING extremes HRES still beats GraphCast/Pangu/FuXi; AI models underestimate frequency and intensity of records, underpredict hot records, overpredict cold records, errors grow with exceedance.

title: Assimilating Observed Surface Pressure Into ML Weather Prediction Models
relevance_note: Slivinski et al.: assimilating surface pressure into ML models produces noise needing spectral filtering — evidence that ML models are not robust to off-manifold inputs.

title: Power Spectra of Physics‐Based and Data‐Driven Ensembles
relevance_note: Rodwell et al., power spectra of physics-based vs data-driven ECMWF ensembles — the spectral diagnostic toolkit, incl. over-dispersion at synoptic scales in physics ensembles.

title: A Practical Probabilistic Benchmark for AI Weather Models
relevance_note: Brenowitz et al., practical probabilistic benchmark: shows EFFECTIVE RESOLUTION modulates ensemble dispersion — the link between blurring and under-dispersion.

title: Distilling Machine Learning’s Added Value: Pareto Fronts in Atmospheric Applications
venue: Artificial Intelligence for the Earth Systems
relevance_note: Beucler et al., Pareto fronts: how to decide whether ML added value is real given cost/complexity. Useful sanity framework for a solo project.

title: Numerical models outperform AI weather forecasts of record-breaking extremes
relevance_note: Preprint of the above with the fuller quantitative statement.

title: Do AI models produce better weather forecasts than physics-based models? A quantitative evaluation case study of Storm Ciarán
relevance_note: Charlton-Perez et al., Storm Ciaran case study: AI models get synoptic structure right but the paper is the standard reference for what they miss at smaller scales.

title: Do data-driven models beat numerical models in forecasting weather extremes? A comparison of IFS HRES, Pangu-Weather, and GraphCast
relevance_note: Olivetti & Messori, GMD: data-driven models mostly beat IFS HRES on global RMSE at 1-10 d for near-surface T and wind extremes, but performance varies strongly by REGION and lead time — best near tropics, weaker elsewhere. Directly relevant to a high-latitude domain.

title: On Some Limitations of Current Machine Learning Weather Prediction Models
relevance_note: THE key defect paper (Bonavita, GRL 2024): Pangu/FourCastNet/GraphCast fail to reproduce sub-synoptic and mesoscale phenomena; lack physical consistency. This is the gap a downscaling layer fills.

title: Validating Deep Learning Weather Forecast Models on Recent High-Impact Extreme Events
venue: Artificial Intelligence for the Earth Systems
relevance_note: Pasche et al., validation of DL forecasts on recent high-impact extremes — case-study-based defect evidence.

title: The Rise of Data-Driven Weather Forecasting: A First Statistical Assessment of Machine Learning–Based Weather Forecasts in an Operational-Like Context
venue: Bulletin of the American Meteorological Society
relevance_note: ECMWF's own first operational-like statistical assessment of ML forecasts (Ben Bouallegue et al., BAMS). The reference for how AI models behave in operations.

title: On some limitations of data-driven weather forecasting models
relevance_note: Preprint version of the above; note its conclusion that ML models already add value as post-processing-like tools.

title: Super-resolving coarse-resolution weather forecasts with flow matching
relevance_note: Delefosse et al.: generative super-resolution as a POST-PROCESSING step decoupled from forecasting; re-coarsening consistency check + spectral diagnostics. A clean methodological template.

title: SwAIther-Precip: Lead-Time-Aware Bias Correction Enables Kilometer-Scale Downscaling of Global AI Precipitation Forecasts over Switzerland
relevance_note: SwAIther-Precip: lead-time-aware bias correction + generative super-resolution of AIFS precip to km scale over Switzerland. CRPS -48% vs raw AIFS; effective resolution ~4 km on a 1 km grid; training across lead times gives a further 13% CRPS gain at day 6. The closest existing analogue to your idea.

authors: Joffrey Dumont Le Brazidec et al.
title: Downscaling weather forecasts from Low- to High-Resolution with Diffusion Models
relevance_note: Dumont Le Brazidec et al.: diffusion downscaling of IFS ensembles 100 km -> 30 km via residual learning; reproduces target power spectra at small scales, physically consistent wind-pressure coupling.

title: HourGlass: A probabilistic data-driven temporal downscaler for global and regional weather forecasting
relevance_note: HourGlass: probabilistic TEMPORAL downscaler applied to AIFS-Single and AIFS-ENS (and MET Norway's Bris). Notes deterministic temporal downscaling produces overly smooth fields.

title: Joint bias correction and downscaling of subseasonal forecasts via diffusion models
relevance_note: Pyrina et al.: joint bias correction and downscaling of subseasonal forecasts via diffusion.

title: Intelligent Shanghai Typhoon Model (ISTM): A Diffusion‐Based Downscaling Emulator From AIFS to Kilometer‐Scale Regional Reanalysis for Typhoon Forecasts
venue: Journal of Geophysical Research Machine Learning and Computation
relevance_note: ISTM: diffusion downscaling emulator from AIFS to km-scale regional reanalysis; cuts 72-h typhoon intensity error ~39.5% vs AIFS. Proof that AIFS-to-km-scale generative downscaling works.

title: Statistical Postprocessing Yields Accurate Probabilistic Forecasts from Artificial Intelligence Weather Models
venue: Artificial Intelligence for the Earth Systems
relevance_note: MOST IMPORTANT FOR YOU. Trotta et al.: applies an EXISTING NWP postprocessing system (IMPROVER) unchanged to AIFS; gets comparable gains to those on HRES/ENS, and blending AIFS with NWP beats either. Direct precedent for your project.

title: Comparative Analysis of Precipitation Forecasts between the ECMWF Artificial Intelligence System (AIFS) and Its Integrated Forecast System (IFS)
relevance_note: Direct AIFS vs IFS precipitation comparison — the AIFS-specific verification you need before choosing a target variable.

title: High-Resolution Probabilistic Data-Driven Weather Modeling with a Stretched-Grid
relevance_note: Nordhagen et al.: probabilistic stretched-grid Nordic model, CRPS-trained in grid-point AND SPECTRAL space. Spectral loss term is NECESSARY for spatially coherent fields; -13% CRPS on 2 m T and -10% on MSLP vs MEPS. Read for the loss-function lesson.

title: A comparison of stretched-grid and limited-area modelling for data-driven regional weather forecasting
relevance_note: Wijnands et al.: head-to-head of stretched-grid vs limited-area for regional data-driven forecasting over Europe; SGM is self-contained and generalises better temporally.

title: A regional high resolution AI weather model for the prediction of atmospheric rivers and extreme precipitation
relevance_note: Bano-Medina et al.: regional stretched-grid AI model at 6 km over western US; captures extreme precipitation that coarse global models underestimate.

title: An artificial intelligence-based limited area model for forecasting of surface meteorological variables
relevance_note: Xu et al.: AI-based limited-area model specifically for SURFACE meteorological variables.

title: Building Machine Learning Limited Area Models: Kilometer-Scale Weather Forecasting in Realistic Settings
relevance_note: Adamov et al.: kilometre-scale ML limited-area models with flexible boundary forcing; systematic ablation of boundary width and graph construction; verified against stations.

title: Regional data-driven weather modeling with a global stretched-grid
relevance_note: Nipen et al.: STRETCHED-GRID extension of AIFS itself — 2.5 km over the Nordics, 31 km globally; pre-trained on 43 yr ERA5 then refined on 3.3 yr MEPS analyses; beats MEPS control and ensemble mean for 2 m temperature. The most directly transferable design for NW Russia.

title: Graph-based Neural Weather Prediction for Limited Area Modeling
relevance_note: Oskarsson et al., Neural-LAM — the original graph-based limited-area formulation and open codebase.

title: STIPP: Space-time in situ postprocessing over the French Alps using proper scoring rules
relevance_note: STIPP: space-time in-situ postprocessing at STATION locations using proper scoring rules; makes hourly ensembles from a 6-hourly deterministic forecast. Closest method template to your station-level task.

title: SEEPS4ALL: an open dataset for the verification of daily precipitation forecasts using station climate statistics
relevance_note: SEEPS4ALL: open dataset for verifying daily precipitation forecasts using station data — relevant given ISD-Lite precip is empty.

title: Advances in land surface forecasting: a comparison of LSTM, gradient boosting, and feed-forward neural networks as prognostic state emulators in a case study with ecLand
relevance_note: Wesselkamp et al.: LSTM vs gradient boosting vs MLP as ecLand land-surface emulators. Relevant because your box is snow/boreal-surface dominated and because it benchmarks exactly the model classes your hardware supports.

title: Generative Data Assimilation of Sparse Weather Station Observations at Kilometer Scales
venue: Journal of Advances in Modeling Earth Systems
relevance_note: Manshausen et al.: generative data assimilation of SPARSE weather station observations at km scale; 10% lower RMSE on held-out stations. Note the caveat of insufficiently dispersive ensembles.

title: Enhancing Regional Climate Downscaling through Advances in Machine Learning
venue: Artificial Intelligence for the Earth Systems
relevance_note: Enhancing regional climate downscaling through advances in ML — bridges the climate-downscaling and NWP-postprocessing literatures.

title: The EUPPBench postprocessing benchmark dataset v1.0
relevance_note: EUPPBench: a European postprocessing BENCHMARK dataset — station-based, directly comparable in spirit to your ISD-Lite setup.

title: Deep learning for post-processing ensemble weather forecasts
venue: Philosophical Transactions of the Royal Society A Mathematical Physical and Engineering Sciences
relevance_note: Groenquist et al.: deep learning for postprocessing ensemble forecasts.

title: Statistical Postprocessing for Weather Forecasts: Review, Challenges, and Avenues in a Big Data World
venue: Bulletin of the American Meteorological Society
relevance_note: Vannitsem et al., BAMS: the standard review of statistical postprocessing. Read before choosing a method.

title: Deep-Learning-Based Gridded Downscaling of Surface Meteorological Variables in Complex Terrain. Part I: Daily Maximum and Minimum 2-m Temperature
venue: Journal of Applied Meteorology and Climatology
relevance_note: Sha et al.: deep-learning gridded downscaling of Tmax/Tmin in COMPLEX TERRAIN — the elevation/representativeness problem you already measured.

title: Neural Networks for Postprocessing Ensemble Weather Forecasts
relevance_note: Rasp & Lerch: distributional regression networks (DRN) for postprocessing ensembles — the workhorse baseline you should implement first. Highly cited, simple, runs on your hardware.
